g.text: steam-overlay-debug
Explains why the Steam overlay is loaded but its InputEvent ring stops draining (#11446), by reading
/proc
/dev/shm
and the overlay binary.
Entry points
State
Core
External
`overlay-scan` · `--pid` / `--comm` / `--cmdline` / `--scan`, `-q`, `--no-live`, `--shm-sample-sec`
`overlay-version` · one binary, a folder or `-r` · `--sort`, `--write-version-md`, `--online-lookup`
`pipx install .` · two console scripts over five plain modules, no package directory
a scan is a point-in-time snapshot · no history, no daemon, no pid file
rows in memory · grouped by sha256, one block per distinct overlay build
`online_lookup` module globals · the manifest is fetched once per run
`VERSION.md` + `version_label/` folders · the only thing ever written
observe the process
measure the ring and the layer
explain it
`/proc/<pid>/maps`, `environ`, `comm`, `cmdline`, `fd` · the whole evidence base
`/dev/shm/GameOverlay_InputEventStream_<pid>` · 524288 B ring + 16 B header
installed Steam tree · `ubuntu12_*`, `steamrt64`, `pressure-vessel-libs` deploy slots
`SteamDatabase/SteamTracking` · `ClientContentLinux.txt` CRC list + client manifest
`debuginfod.steamos.cloud` · build id → debuginfo, 404 for client overlays
`/proc` walk · `pids_for_scan`: SHM clients first, then any mapping
`maps` parse · `map_files/<vma>` for deleted .so, dedupe by inode
`_process_role` · launcher / game / other · game means it owns an InputEvent ring
`version.py` · PE/ELF, Build ID, FileVersion, toolchain, slot
`discover_shm_path` · name, else a 524304/524288 map, fd by size
header `kind == 2` at +16 and cursor ≤ capacity · otherwise keep looking
`probe_pid` · uint32 at +4 twice, ring % full
`vulkan_layer_manifest` · ENABLE/DISABLE env, `VK_*_PATH`
`_overlay_graphics_report` · Vulkan layer vs preload vs Wine
`print_scan_deduped` · one block per sha256, then every pid
`_print_launcher_game_check` · shell build vs game build
`online_lookup` · CRC32 vs SteamTracking, debuginfod by id
`-q` · build id, injector, APIs, frame-loop yes/no
same analyzer, different question
only processes that map an overlay
the mapping alone does not say who runs the game
read the bytes the process actually has mapped
a same-size map is not proof
only a plausible ring gets sampled
frame heartbeat next to layer policy
the launcher is the usual red herring
the CRC is the only cheap identity across machines
online detail is optional, the verdict is local
a command picks a report
everything is read, never written
one row per build, one snapshot per run
